title: Choose the layout for a single update page
question: The roll dealt three layouts for the page an ICT Trends update opens. Keep the lead, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: Changelog entry
options.lineage: Real product changelogs on Refero: Cycle, Family, Womp
options.thesis: Each update is a dated entry in NICTD's record, read like a product changelog.
options.viewport: A left rail holds the date set large with the category under it; the right column carries the headline, photo and text, with the neighbouring updates listed beneath.
options.risk: With one short entry the rail can feel empty unless the date and the neighbours carry real weight.

options.label: Editorial split
options.lineage: Editorial article pages on Dribbble and Refero (New Balance, Glukhovsky)
options.thesis: The update opens like a feature story: its headline set beside its photograph.
options.viewport: The first screen splits in two: category, date, a large headline and the opening sentence on the left; the photo fills the right half to the edge.
options.risk: A short update under a big feature layout can read as more news than it is.

options.label: Gazette notice
options.lineage: Government gazettes and ONS statistical release pages
options.thesis: Each update is issued as a numbered public notice in the national ICT record.
options.viewport: A notice header with its number for the year and its release date, then the title, the text, and the photo set as a captioned plate.
options.risk: Official framing can feel bureaucratic, and it claims an authority the demonstration data has not earned yet.
